transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

The E:15 code on your Bosch SMV4HTX31E indicates that the water-protection system has detected water in the bottom of the machine (the base pan). This is a safety feature designed to prevent flooding if there is an internal leak. When this activates, the drain pump runs continuously to remove the water and the machine locks out. 1. There is a genuine leak inside the dishwasher (e.g., from the door seal, spray arm, or pump seals) that has filled the base tray.
2. Before we look for leaks, we need to confirm if the base is actually wet. Please tilt the machine back slightly (ensure it's unplugged and you have help due to weight) to check the base tray. Is there water present in the base, or does it appear dry?
I can't tilt it, it's an integrated unit under the worktop and the kitchen is fitted. I did look through a gap in the plinth with a torch though and can see a little shine of water in the base tray.

Seeing that shine of water suggests the anti-flood system has done its job: it detected moisture and ran the pump to clear it. Because you can't tilt the machine, we need to work out where the leak is coming from so the tray doesn't just fill up again. The most common causes for an integrated dishwasher with a wet base are:
1. An internal leak (often from the circulation pump seal or a loose sump hose) that drips directly into the base tray.
2. A door seal issue where water escapes during washing and runs down to the bottom.
3. Less commonly, a split spray arm firing water at the door. To separate these, we need to check if there is also water in the main tub (above the filter) or just in the base tray below it. Please remove the lower rack and twist out the cylindrical filter at the bottom of the tub. Look into the sump with a torch:
• Is there standing water in the main tub, or does it look dry?
• Can you see any debris (glass, bones, food) stuck around the small impeller blades inside? This tells us if the leak is coming from above (tub/seal/spray arm) or below (pump/hose into the base).
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
I've taken the filter out and it's fairly clean. I'm not sure about standing water in the tub or anything round the impeller, I can't tell from looking. The pump is still humming away.

Since we cannot easily drain the base without tilting the machine (which isn't possible with your fitted kitchen), we need to identify where the leak is coming from so it doesn't just fill up again. 1. An internal leak (e.g., from the circulation pump seal or a sump hose) dripping directly into the base tray.
2. A door seal issue where water escapes during washing and runs down to the bottom. To separate these, please open the door and inspect the rubber gasket (seal) around the tub opening and the inside of the door. Is there any moisture or dripping on that seal, or does it look completely dry? This will tell us if the leak is coming from the door area or from deep inside the machine.
The door seal looks okay to me, no moisture or drips that I can see. Pump's still humming.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The most common cause for this on integrated Bosch dishwashers is a worn seal on the circulation pump (which sits at the bottom of the tub) or a loose internal hose dripping directly into the base pan. Because you cannot tilt the machine to drain it, we need to confirm where the water is coming from so it doesn't just fill up again. 1. Does water drip from the bottom edge of the door onto the floor? (This would point to the door seal or spray arm).
2. If there is no leak at the door, it suggests an internal component failure (likely the pump seal). In that case, because you cannot access the base pan to drain and dry it without removing the appliance from under the worktop, this will require a qualified engineer to dismantle the machine and replace the faulty part.
No water on the floor at all, nothing dripping from the door. So is it an engineer then? I can't pull the unit out or take the plinth off without wrecking it.

Yes, this requires an engineer. The E:15 code suggests the anti-flood system has detected water in the base pan and locked the machine out to prevent flooding. The leak is internal—most commonly from a worn seal on the circulation pump at the bottom of the tub. 1. Safely disconnect the appliance (electricity, water, and waste).
2. Remove it from under the worktop.
3. Dismantle the base to drain the water and dry the area.
4. Replace the faulty internal component (likely the pump seal or pump assembly).
5. Reinstall and test. Please do not try to run the machine again, as this will just refill the base pan and trigger the fault repeatedly.
